For $M\dot v+h=\bar B u$, the following quantities have distinct meanings.
Evaluate every row at the same declared state and in the same coordinates.

| Quantity | Definition | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Applied Generalized Load | $\tau_{\mathrm{ID}}=M\dot v+h$ | Net input required by the declared inverse-dynamics model |
| Resultant Generalized Load | $\tau_{\text{total}}=M\dot v$ | Right-hand side of the acceleration balance |
| Pointwise Drift (ZTCF) | $\tau_{\mathrm{ZTCF}}=-h(z,v)$ | Autonomous load with declared control zero; includes gravity once |
| Pointwise Control (ZVCF) | $\tau_{\mathrm{ZVCF}}=\bar B u$ | Declared control under the ZVCF evaluation protocol |
| Zero-Velocity Baseline | $-h(z,0)$ | Configuration-dependent bias at zero velocity; not ZVCF control |
| Velocity-Dependent Drift | $-[h(z,v)-h(z,0)]$ | Difference under that reset, including retained damping |
| Declared Input Contribution | $\tau_{\text{input}}=\bar B u$ | Same control channel as ZVCF; not muscle-force allocation |

: Generalized-Load Bookkeeping {#tbl-taxonomy}

At a fixed achieved state, $\tau_{\text{total}}=\tau_{\mathrm{ZTCF}}+\tau_{\mathrm{ZVCF}}$
because $M\dot v=-h+\bar B u$ is affine in the declared control. Do not add
integrated counterfactual trajectories as though they superposed. In redundant
coordinates, constraint forces require their own balance; uniqueness of net
reduced torque does not establish unique actuator, muscle, or bilateral
hand-force allocation [@lynch2017modern].

For a chosen, identifiable reaction output in a fixed smooth contact mode,
substituting acceleration into the reaction equations can yield
$r(x,u)=r_d(x)+R_u(x)u$. A same-state subtraction then gives
$r(x,u)-r(x,0)=R_u(x)u$. Declare the reference point, frame, sign and force/moment
components. The result for a wrench is not obtained by relabeling an actuator
torque. Changes of mode, friction branches or unidentified internal forces
require additional treatment.

There is no universal fourth "mixed force" equal to total minus pointwise ZTCF
drift minus pointwise ZVCF control minus a zero-velocity baseline. Mixing
forward ZTCF trajectories with instantaneous operands subtracts overlapping
terms at different states. To investigate interactions, define two interventions
and a common outcome $Y$: the contrast
$Y_{11}-Y_{10}-Y_{01}+Y_{00}$ measures nonadditivity for those interventions and
that outcome. It is not a new physical force or a unique anatomical cause.

### How Geometry, Energy, and Torque Work Together

Past torque changes the present configuration, speed, and elastic deformation.
Those states change both the drift and the input-to-acceleration map. Current
torque then acts through that changed geometry. A shaft can store and return
energy, but it does not create energy; compare complete endpoint energy and
work balances when changing shaft or timing parameters.

For time-independent kinetic and potential energy and ideal stationary
constraints, the total mechanical energy satisfies

$$
\dot E=v^\mathsf{T}\bar B u-v^\mathsf{T}d+P_{\mathrm{external}},
\qquad E=\tfrac12v^\mathsf{T}Mv+V.
$$

In this energy balance, $d$ denotes the declared dissipative loads and
$P_{\mathrm{external}}$ the power of the remaining external ports.
If an external load was absorbed into $h$ in the dynamics convention, separate
it out before using this balance; do not count it in both $d$ and
$P_{\mathrm{external}}$. Conservative forces represented by $V$ are already
accounted for through stored energy.

The inertial/Coriolis terms redistribute motion consistently with this balance;
their individual magnitudes are not independent energy sources. At an internal
interface, equal and opposite wrenches cancel in the whole-system balance but
can transfer power between segments. A segment slowing down does not by itself
show that its energy went into the club: examine joint force power, moment
power, elastic storage and external work [@featherstone2008rigid].

A torque's sign alone does not identify braking. For one angular coordinate,
$P=\tau\dot q$ is negative when the torque opposes velocity. Zero power does
not imply zero muscle effort, and large normal force can redirect motion while
doing little instantaneous work at a specified moving point. This distinction
connects hand-path geometry, energy transfer and delivery without conflating
force, impulse, work, tissue load and neural strategy.
